/-!
# Conjecture 6.62

by V. P. Shunkov

Is a (conjugacy, $p$-conjugacy) biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup ($p$-subgroup)? There are affirmative answers for conjugacy biprimitively
finite $p$-groups and for $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite groups (V. P. Shunkov,
*Algebra and Logic*, **9**, no. 4 (1970), 291–297; **11**, no. 4 (1972), 260–272;
**12**, no. 5 (1973), 347–353), while the statement does not hold for arbitrary periodic
groups, see Archive, 3.9.

A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. It is *conjugacy
biprimitively finite* (a *Shunkov group*) if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
*conjugate* elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. For a prime
$p$, it is *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any
two conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. Groups are not
assumed to be periodic. A *maximal subgroup* is a maximal proper subgroup, i.e. a coatom of
the lattice of subgroups.

The question is read as three questions, one for each way of resolving the parentheticals:
"biprimitively finite" with "finite maximal subgroup", "conjugacy biprimitively finite" with
"finite maximal subgroup", and "$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite" with "finite maximal
subgroup that is a $p$-subgroup". In the last reading the maximal subgroup is a maximal
subgroup of $G$ that happens to be a $p$-group, not a Sylow $p$-subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.isConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (hG : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) :

  fun H hH x y hx hy _ => hG H hH x y hx hy

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite.isPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite
    (hG : IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy hxy => hG H hH x y (hx ▸ hp) (hy ▸ hp) hxy

blocks.name: IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite.isPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite
blocks.text:
/-- For a prime $p$, a conjugacy biprimitively finite group is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively
finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite.isPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite
    (hG : IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy hxy => hG H hH x y (hx ▸ hp) (hy ▸ hp) hxy

blocks.docstring:
Let $p$ be a prime. Is a $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup which is a $p$-subgroup? The statement is quantified over all primes $p$.

This is the reading of the question with the parenthetical alternatives "$p$-conjugacy" and
"$p$-subgroup". The maximal subgroup is a maximal proper subgroup of $G$ that is a
$p$-group; it is not a Sylow $p$-subgroup (a maximal element among the $p$-subgroups), since
with that reading every infinite elementary abelian $q$-group, $q \ne p$, would be a trivial
counterexample. The case $p = 2$ was answered affirmatively by Shunkov, see
`kourovka.«6.62».variants.two_conjugacy`.

blocks.docstring:
The statement does not hold for arbitrary periodic groups (see Archive, 3.9): it is not true
that every periodic group with a finite maximal subgroup is finite. For example, in a Tarski
monster every non-trivial proper subgroup has prime order, so it is a finite maximal
subgroup of an infinite periodic group.

the lattice of subgroups.

The question is read as three questions, one for each way of resolving the parentheticals:
"biprimitively finite" with "finite maximal subgroup", "conjugacy biprimitively finite" with
"finite maximal subgroup", and "$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite" with "finite maximal
subgroup that is a $p$-subgroup". In the last reading the maximal subgroup is a maximal
subgroup of $G$ that happens to be a $p$-group, not a Sylow $p$-subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.62»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup $H \le G$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* (a *Shunkov group*) if for every finite
subgroup $H \le G$, any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *$p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite* if for every finite subgroup
$H \le G$, any two conjugate elements of order $p$ in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      orderOf x = p → orderOf y = p → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A finite group is biprimitively finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.of_finite [Finite G] : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A biprimitively finite group is conjugacy biprimitively finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.isConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (hG : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) :
    IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy _ => hG H hH x y hx hy

/-- For a prime $p$, a conjugacy biprimitively finite group is $p$-conjugacy biprimitively
finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite.isPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite
    (hG : IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) :
    IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy hxy => hG H hH x y (hx ▸ hp) (hy ▸ hp) hxy

/--
Is a biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup?

This is the reading of the question with both parenthetical alternatives omitted. A maximal
subgroup of $G$ is a maximal proper subgroup, i.e. a coatom of the lattice of subgroups
of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
Is a conjugacy biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup?

This is the reading of the question with the first parenthetical alternative "conjugacy".
The case of $p$-groups was answered affirmatively by Shunkov, see
`kourovka.«6.62».variants.conjugacy_p_group`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
Let $p$ be a prime. Is a $p$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup which is a $p$-subgroup? The statement is quantified over all primes $p$.

This is the reading of the question with the parenthetical alternatives "$p$-conjugacy" and
"$p$-subgroup". The maximal subgroup is a maximal proper subgroup of $G$ that is a
$p$-group; it is not a Sylow $p$-subgroup (a maximal element among the $p$-subgroups), since
with that reading every infinite elementary abelian $q$-group, $q \ne p$, would be a trivial
counterexample. The case $p = 2$ was answered affirmatively by Shunkov, see
`kourovka.«6.62».variants.two_conjugacy`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite p G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup p M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
For every prime $p$, a conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-group is finite if it has a finite
maximal subgroup. This is the affirmative answer for conjugacy biprimitively finite $p$-groups
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **9**, no. 4 (1970), 291–297). It is a special case of
`kourovka.«6.62».parts.ii`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.conjugacy_p_group : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup p G →
      IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
A $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite group is finite if it has a finite maximal subgroup
which is a $2$-subgroup. This is the affirmative answer for $2$-conjugacy biprimitively finite
groups, i.e. the case $p = 2$ of `kourovka.«6.62».parts.iii`
(V. P. Shunkov, *Algebra and Logic*, **11**, no. 4 (1972), 260–272; **12**, no. 5 (1973),
347–353).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.two_conjugacy : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite 2 G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup 2 M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
The statement does not hold for arbitrary periodic groups (see Archive, 3.9): it is not true
that every periodic group with a finite maximal subgroup is finite. For example, in a Tarski
monster every non-trivial proper subgroup has prime order, so it is a finite maximal
subgroup of an infinite periodic group.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.62».variants.periodic :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G →
      (∃ M : Subgroup G, IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M) → Finite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.62»

items: Groups are not assumed periodic in parts.i–iii (and in the variants), following the table and the notebook's wording 'group'; definitions of (conjugacy) biprimitively finite groups make sense for arbitrary groups.

Definitions of the three finiteness classes follow the standard literature definitions (Shunkov): quantify over all finite subgroups H (including H = 1), in N_G(H)/H, elements of prime order given by (orderOf x).Prime, conjugacy by IsConj, 'generate a finite subgroup' by Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y}). In the conjugacy/p-conjugacy definitions the order condition is stated for both elements, which is redundant given IsConj but literal.

'Maximal subgroup' is IsCoatom M in Subgroup G (maximal proper subgroup). 'Finite maximal p-subgroup' in parts.iii/two_conjugacy is IsCoatom M ∧ Finite M ∧ IsPGroup p M, not a Sylow p-subgroup, as the table requires.
parts.iii and conjugacy_p_group put the universal quantifier over primes p inside answer(...) ↔ ∀ p, ..., so a single yes/no answer covers all primes.
The two solved variants use the answer(True) ↔ ... idiom (as in Paper/LatinSquare.lean); the negative periodic variant is stated as ¬ ∀ ..., per CONTRIBUTING for statements solved negatively.

Three sorry-free @[category API] lemmas were added as basic tests of the definitions (biprimitively finite ⇒ conjugacy ⇒ p-conjugacy; finite groups are biprimitively finite). The definitions live in the problem file rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib, as in Kourovka/1_40.lean, since the task confines all work to the candidate file.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates compiled and agree on the mathematics; differences were cosmetic (naming, one-vs-two order hypotheses on conjugate elements, ¬∀ / answer(False) / ∃ for the periodic remark, presence of API lemmas). Final file composed from c07 (defs inlined without the extra abbrev, three sorry-free API/test lemmas, six slot theorems) and compiles with only 'sorry' warnings. Interpretive points a human should know: (1) the notebook does not define its terms; the file uses the standard Shunkov definitions and, following the decomposition table, quantifies 'p-conjugacy biprimitively finite' over all finite subgroups H (some literature may restrict H to finite p-subgroups — c01 flagged this too; the table's choice gives a stronger hypothesis, hence a weaker question). (2) '(p-subgroup)' is read as 'finite maximal proper subgroup that is a p-group', not Sylow-style; the Sylow reading is trivially false (infinite elementary abelian q-group, q ≠ p) so the table's reading is the only coherent one. (3) The 2-conjugacy affirmative answer is read as the p = 2 instance of parts.iii; the stronger reading without the 2-group hypothesis is actually false (Tarski monster for an odd prime is vacuously 2-conjugacy biprimitively finite), so it cannot be what Shunkov proved. (4) No periodicity is assumed in parts.i–iii, consistent with the literature treating non-periodic Shunkov groups; note an infinite group with a finite maximal subgroup is necessarily finitely generated with finite abelianization, so no trivial non-periodic counterexample exists. (5) Solved variants use the answer(True) ↔ idiom; the negative periodic remark uses ¬∀ per CONTRIBUTING.

$-subgroup)? There are affirmative answers for conjugacy biprimitively finite $p\hskip0.2ex $-groups and for 2-conjugacy biprimitively finite groups (V. P. Shunkov, Algebra and Logic, 9, no. 4 (1970), 291–297; 11, no. 4 (1972), 260–272; 12, no. 5 (1973), 347–353), while the statement does not hold for arbitrary periodic groups, see Archive, 3.9.
